extracted.intended_audience: general readers and journalists interested in media ethics/photojournalism
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and practices for editing, accepting, and retracting news photographs — what edits are permissible, what constitutes doctoring, and editorial responses when manipulation is discovered.

rubrics_metrics.name: No content-altering doctoring
rubrics_metrics.description: A photographer is never allowed to change content; you can't add information; you can't take away things.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any manipulation that changes the substantive content of an image is forbidden. Example in article: an altered photo intensified smoke in Beirut; another altered photo showed three flares when the original showed one flare — both are content changes and thus unacceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible cosmetic corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: While it's permissible to change the appearance of photos -- to correct a purple skin tone, for example -- such changes must not alter content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed edits are limited to appearance/corrective adjustments (color balance, exposure, minor cosmetic fixes) that do not add, remove, or materially change elements of the scene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zero-tolerance policy for doctoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Reuters has zero tolerance to doctoring photos this way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When manipulation is detected, the agency enforces strict consequences (e.g., no longer accepting pictures from the photographer). This policy is applied decisively to preserve credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate retraction upon discovery
rubrics_metrics.description: The Beirut smoke photo was retracted immediately after it was transmitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Images found to be doctored should be withdrawn promptly from distribution and clients should be notified as soon as manipulation is confirmed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial review responsibility and failure modes
rubrics_metrics.description: "This one slipped through the system," — a photo editor looked at it, coded it, and sent it to clients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial workflow must include review and coding of images before distribution; failures in that process (allowing a doctored image to be published) are recognized as systemic lapses and should trigger procedural fixes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement by withdrawal of photographer's work
rubrics_metrics.description: After a second photo was found to be altered, Reuters withdrew all of Hajj's photographs from its database and said it would no longer accept pictures from the photographer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeat or severe breaches lead to broader enforcement actions such as removing a photographer's archive and banning future contributions to protect the agency's integrity.
